successCriteria.description: The LeaveType enum is exported from src/shared/types/index.ts and exposes exactly the six members ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY (matching the reconciled architecture), each usable as a typed value.
The LeaveRequestStatus enum is exported from src/shared/types/index.ts and exposes exactly the five members DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED.

The EmploymentStatus enum is exported from src/shared/types/index.ts and exposes exactly the three members ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED (no ON_LEAVE or SUSPENDED), matching the architecture's Employee lifecycle.

Each of NotFoundError, ValidationError, UnauthorizedError, ConflictError is exported from src/shared/errors.ts, extends Error, is constructible with a message, and exposes a readonly statusCode property with the correct value (404, 400, 401, 409 respectively); instances satisfy `instanceof Error`.

BaseRepository<T> is exported from src/shared/base.repository.ts as an abstract generic class whose public surface includes findById, findAll(filters?), create, update, and delete with the exact return types (Promise<T|null>, Promise<T[]>, Promise<T>, Promise<T>, Promise<void>); the class cannot be instantiated directly (abstract) but a concrete subclass can be constructed.

BaseRepository obtains its database access by importing the existing `pool` from src/shared/db/connection.ts and exposing it as a protected property typed as pg.Pool, so concrete subclasses can issue queries through it without re-importing the pool.

Unit tests exist under tests/unit/shared/ (files ending in .test.ts) covering the error classes (assert correct statusCode, message propagation, instanceof Error) and BaseRepository (using a concrete test subclass with the pg pool mocked, verifying create/update/findById/findAll/delete delegate to the pool and return the expected shapes).
The phase compiles cleanly under `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) and `npm test` passes with no type errors, satisfying the strict-mode TypeScript configuration and the no-any constraint.

constraints: No use of `any` anywhere in the new files or tests; the `findAll(filters?: Record<string, unknown>)` parameter must remain `unknown`-typed, and any narrowing must use type guards (HARNESS no-any, high severity).

All database access in BaseRepository must go through the repository pattern using the imported `pool`; no inline SQL or direct pg calls outside the repository abstraction (HARNESS no-direct-db-outside-repository, critical severity; GP-001).
New code must compile under the existing strict TypeScript config (strict: true, strictNullChecks, no implicit any, ES2022 target, commonjs module, baseUrl ./src) without modifying tsconfig.json.

Test files must live under tests/ and end in .test.ts to match the Jest testMatch glob (**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)); ts-jest compiles them at test time even though tsconfig excludes tests from the build.

Enum values must follow the reconciled architecture, superseding the PLAN.md task description: LeaveType has 6 members (adds UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY) and EmploymentStatus has 3 members (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED — no ON_LEAVE/SUSPENDED). LeaveRequestStatus has 5 members as stated.
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens in the new files or tests (HARNESS no-hardcoded-secrets, critical severity).
outOfScope: Concrete domain repositories (EmployeeRepository, PolicyRepository, BalanceRepository, LeaveRepository) and their table-specific query methods — these are Phases 2-5.
Domain model interfaces (Employee, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest) and their DTOs — Phases 2-5.
LeaveService business logic, Fastify routes, route-to-statusCode error mapping, RBAC middleware, and audit logging — Phases 6-8.
Database migrations/schema creation and any actual PostgreSQL connection at test time — BaseRepository tests must mock the pool, not hit a real database.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum's member set is closed and immutable at exactly ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY; no other leave-type values may exist in the codebase, and every later-phase domain model that references a leave type must use this enum rather than a raw string.

The enum's member set is closed at exactly DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED and encodes the full LeaveRequest lifecycle (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→(APPROVED|REJECTED); APPROVED→CANCELLED); no additional status values may be introduced.
The enum's member set is closed at exactly ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED, matching the architecture's Employee lifecycle; ON_LEAVE and SUSPENDED must not be present.

entityInvariants.entity: Shared error classes (NotFoundError, ValidationError, UnauthorizedError, ConflictError)
entityInvariants.invariant: Each error class extends Error, carries a stable readonly statusCode (404/400/401/409 respectively) that does not change between instances, and preserves the constructor-provided message on the Error.message property so callers can discriminate by type (instanceof) and read statusCode for HTTP mapping.

BaseRepository is abstract and generic: it cannot be instantiated directly and must be subclassed to provide a concrete T and table binding; its five CRUD methods (findById, findAll, create, update, delete) constitute the complete data-access contract that every later-phase concrete repository inherits, and all database interaction flows through the protected pool-backed db property rather than external imports.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.findById(id) — retrieve a single entity by its identifier
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the entity when found or null when no row matches; must not throw on a missing row (null is the not-found signal). Database/query errors propagate as thrown errors.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.findAll(filters?) — retrieve a collection of entities, optionally narrowed by opaque filter criteria
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array (empty when no matches) rather than null; filter values are typed as unknown and must be narrowed/handled safely without any-casts. Database errors propagate as thrown errors.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.create(entity) — persist a new entity from a partial representation and return the persisted record
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the fully-formed persisted entity; constraint/conflict failures from the database propagate as thrown errors (later phases may wrap these into ConflictError, but the base layer surfaces the underlying error).

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.update(id, updates) — apply a partial update to an existing entity and return the updated record
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the updated entity; behavior when the target id does not exist must be defined by the implementation (return null or throw) but must be consistent and documented — later phases rely on this contract for NotFoundError mapping.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.delete(id) — remove an entity by identifier
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Resolves with void on success; behavior when the target id does not exist must be defined by the implementation (silent success or throw) and remain consistent for later-phase callers. Database errors propagate as thrown errors.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: BaseRepository must import and reuse the already-exported `pool` (a pg.Pool instance) from src/shared/db/connection.ts as its protected db property, rather than constructing a new Pool or duplicating connection logic; the import must resolve under the baseUrl ./src module resolution.

The enum member sets must match the reconciled architecture in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: LeaveType = annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity (6), LeaveRequestStatus = DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED (5), Employee/EmploymentStatus lifecycle = ACTIVE/INACTIVE/TERMINATED (3). This supersedes the PLAN.md Phase 1 task description where it differs.

BaseRepository must embody GP-001 (repository pattern): it is the sole channel through which database access occurs, and later-phase services/controllers will depend on repository interfaces rather than touching the pool directly; the base class must not expose raw pool mutation methods that bypass the CRUD contract.

All new source files must typecheck under the existing tsconfig.json strict settings (strict: true, strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, ES2022/commonjs, baseUrl ./src) without requiring tsconfig changes; test files are excluded from the build compile but must still be valid under ts-jest's strict compilation at test time.

Test files must be discoverable by the existing jest.config.js (preset ts-jest, testMatch **/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js), moduleDirectories node_modules+src) — placing them under tests/unit/shared/ with .test.ts extension satisfies the glob without config changes.

integrationPoints.why: BaseRepository imports `pool` from this module as its protected db property; this is the single existing database integration point the new code depends on.

integrationPoints.target: Later-phase concrete repositories (EmployeeRepository, PolicyRepository, BalanceRepository, LeaveRepository — Phases 2-5)
integrationPoints.why: BaseRepository<T> is the base class every concrete repository extends, and the shared enums/errors are imported by every domain model and service in Phases 2-7; this phase establishes the contract those phases depend on.

integrationPoints.target: Phase 6 LeaveService and Phase 7 route error mapping
integrationPoints.why: The four error classes and their statusCode values are consumed by LeaveService (Phase 6) for typed error throwing and by the Fastify route layer (Phase 7) for HTTP status mapping; the class statusCode values (404/400/401/409) are the canonical source, with Phase 7's 403 route mapping being a route-layer detail for UnauthorizedError, not a change to the class.
